skill.name: prove-it-ran
skill.description: Verify that tests, builds and checks actually ran and exercised the changed code, before claiming a task is done. Use before reporting completion, or when asked to prove tests ran or verify a fix.
skill.summary: Verify completion claims with fresh test results, regression checks, exit codes, and explicit evidence.
skill.author: agentkitco

security_audit.summary: All six static findings are false positives involving Markdown formatting, scoped verification commands, or evidence-reporting instructions. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential collection, exfiltration, or malicious command execution. Temporary source changes require care, but the procedure explicitly limits their scope and requires restoration.

4. **Confirm it covers the change.** For a bug fix, the test must fail without the fix: temporarily

7. **Report in a table** and be explicit about anything you did not or could not run.

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks delimit Markdown containing echo $?, which reads the previous command's exit status. This is verification guidance, not Ruby execution or command injection.
The inline git stash reference supports a regression check limited to the source change, followed by restoration. No shell substitution or arbitrary payload appears.
Backticks mark skip labels and a read-only rg search for disabled tests. The command uses a literal search pattern without dynamic shell evaluation.
Lines 29-35 contain a fenced Markdown report table with placeholder commands and example results. The fence is documentation syntax, not executable backtick substitution.
The line requests a verification table and disclosure of checks that could not run. It contains no host enumeration or system reconnaissance.
The rule requires command output or an explicit statement that verification was not performed. It does not request system information or reconnaissance.

content.user_title: Verify Tests Ran Before Reporting Completion
content.value_statement: Completion claims can hide skipped tests, stale results, or checks that never exercised a change. This skill guides fresh verification and reports evidence for each claim.
actual_capabilities: Map completion claims to fresh verification commands and captured output.
Check test counts, exit codes, file discovery, and test configuration.
Guide regression checks that fail without the fix and pass after restoration.
Search for skipped tests and focused-test markers.
Include project-defined lint, type checks, and builds in verification.
Report commands, evidence, and unverified claims in a table.
limitations: Provides instructions rather than a bundled test runner or verification script.
Depends on available project commands, dependencies, and execution permissions.
Cannot verify device-dependent, credential-dependent, or production checks without the required environment.
Cannot guarantee complete test coverage or prove that software has no defects.

use_cases.title: Validate a Bug Fix
use_cases.description: Confirm that a regression test fails without the fix and passes after restoration before closing a bug.

use_cases.title: Review Completion Evidence
use_cases.description: Compare implementation claims with fresh test counts, exit codes, and skipped-test evidence during review.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Release Checkpoint
use_cases.description: Collect build, lint, type-check, and test results while identifying checks blocked by missing infrastructure.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Single Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify that [test command] actually runs the intended test. Report the test count, exit code, and any skipped tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: confirm a specific test executed.

prompt_templates.title: Check Completion Claims
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these claims: [claims]. Run the relevant project checks and report exact commands, fresh evidence, and anything not verified.

prompt_templates.title: Prove a Regression Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify that [regression test] fails without [fix] and passes with it. Preserve unrelated edits and restore temporary changes. Report any verification limits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: establish that a test detects the original defect.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Release Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [release changes] using project-defined tests, lint, type checks, and builds. Check discovery and skips. Report failures, evidence, and environment-dependent gaps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: consolidate evidence across multiple checks.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: prove that a regression test detects the original bug.
output: Claim: the regression test detects the defect.
Evidence: one test failed without the fix and passed after the fix was restored.
Exit codes: 1 before restoration and 0 afterward.
Verified: yes for the targeted regression; the wider suite was not run.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: assess a test command that exits successfully but finds no tests.
output: Evidence: the command exited with code 0, but the runner reported zero tests.
Verified: no; the command did not exercise the changed code.
Next check: confirm the working directory, configuration, and test filename pattern.

best_practices: Run checks after the latest edits and retain exact commands with their output.
Isolate temporary source reversions, preserve unrelated work, and confirm restoration before continuing.
Separate verified claims from blocked checks and document how remaining checks can be performed.
anti_patterns: Treating zero tests, skipped tests, or stale output as proof of success.
Changing tests, snapshots, or thresholds solely to make checks pass.
Calling failures pre-existing without confirming them on a clean checkout.

faq.question: What does this skill verify?
faq.answer: It guides checks that commands ran, tests exercised the change, and completion claims have recorded evidence.

faq.question: Does it include its own test runner?
faq.answer: No. It uses the project tools and commands available to the assistant.

faq.question: Does a zero exit code prove tests passed?
faq.answer: No. The runner must also discover tests, execute the relevant cases, and expose skipped or excluded checks.

faq.question: Why test without the fix?
faq.answer: A failure without the fix shows that the regression test can detect the original defect.

faq.question: What happens when a check needs credentials or hardware?
faq.answer: The report marks the check as not verified and explains how the user can perform it.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: The report lists all three as supported tools. Actual verification depends on their access to project files and command execution.
